milestone: Horizen Pilot — Pulse admission reads receipted constitutional state instead of reinterpreting Horizen on every render
problem: Every surface downstream of the Pulse ceremony (PulseTransparencyToggle, the Verify status route) derived its current-state display by re-parsing Horizen's raw get_onboarding_status response at read time — first via a prose regex classifier, then (once that classifier's cross-capability veto bug was fixed the same day) via a structured-first classifier that still ran fresh, on every 'Check status again' click. The partner's response WAS the runtime's source of truth for what the UI showed, rather than a fact the runtime verified once and then recorded.
observedFailure: The same rendered surface simultaneously showed a local projection of 'Pulse is not enrolled' alongside an authoritative Horizen response reporting enrolled=true — because the projection was reconstructed from prose on every read rather than read from a settled record.

Fixing the immediate classifier bug (an unrelated capability's own 'next step: enroll' text vetoing Pulse's own positive evidence) closed that specific defect, but every future 'Check status' click still re-ran full classification against live partner text — the SAME class of risk (a parsing regression, a partner wording change, a cross-capability veto nobody has found yet) remained architecturally live, only patched at its one known trigger.

There was no way to ask 'does Horizen still agree with what we already decided?' without re-deciding from scratch — verification and reconciliation were the same code path, so a reconciliation read could silently overwrite a settled CONFIRMED outcome with a misclassification, and there was no record of what was actually verified at confirmation time versus what a later read happened to say.
rootCauses: No receipt captured WHAT was verified at the moment of confirmation — horizen_pulse_authorized's actionInput carried identifiers (tokenId, network, controllerWallet) but not the structured facts (pulseEnrolled, pulseCommitmentRecorded, verifiablePnlRegistered, endpointWarning) that justified the CONFIRMED transition, nor a commitment over the complete source response.

verifyHorizenTransparencyActivation conflated two distinct operations — verify-and-transition (legitimate for a row that has not yet confirmed) and read-for-display (which should never re-run classification against live prose) — into one function, so every caller wanting 'what is the current Pulse state' had no choice but to re-derive it from a fresh or cached partner read.

External-network state (a partner's HTTP/MCP response) was treated as directly authoritative for the RUNTIME's rendering decision, rather than as evidence to be verified once and converted into a constitutional fact via a receipted transition — the ordinary multichain-app pattern of asking a network what reality is at render time, applied to a domain (constitutional admission state) that has its own receipted ledger for exactly this purpose.
resolution: writeConfirmedPulseActivation now builds and persists a complete evidence commitment on CONFIRMED — network, tokenId, controllerWallet, authorizationId, every structured fact (pulseEnrolled/pulseCommitmentRecorded/verifiablePnlRegistered/endpointWarning), a sha256 commitment over the COMPLETE source response (never the pre-existing 500-char partnerStatus truncation), a verification timestamp, and a named verifier/policy version — carried in horizen_pulse_authorized's actionInput.evidence.

Added two fine-grained, independently-gated receipt types alongside the existing horizen_pulse_authorized: pulse_enrollment_verified (fires whenever the transition confirms) and pulse_commitment_verified (fires only when the SAME confirmation also verified pulseCommitmentRecorded) — additive, never replacing the existing receipt, so every current reader (the journey-state route's hasReceipt('horizen_pulse_authorized') among them) is unaffected.

Added getPulseAuthorizationEvidence — a three-valued reader (found / not-found / read-failed, never conflated) of the receipted evidence by receiptRef — and wired verify/status/route.ts's already-confirmed-and-enriched fast path to serve structuredStatus from it instead of leaving the field undefined. This is a pure activity_receipts row read, not a partner call, so the pre-existing zero-latency short-circuit is unchanged.

Added reconcilePulseConstitutionalState as a SEPARATE primitive (never the same code path as verify-and-transition) for checking an already-CONFIRMED row against a fresh partner read: agreement records the check and changes nothing else; disagreement writes a NEW reconciliation_discrepancy_recorded receipt naming exactly which fields disagreed and leaves `state` untouched. Exposed via POST /api/journey/moneypenny-horizen/verify/reconcile. Deliberately not wired into any automatic cadence this pass — see rejectedApproaches.

Rebuilt activity_receipts_action_type_check (migration 20260930002000) with the three new action types, per the existing 2026-07-15 constraint-drift incident's own regression guard (tests/activity-receipts-action-type-parity.test.ts).
rejectedApproaches: Wiring reconciliation directly into the existing 'already confirmed and enriched' fast path on every 'Check status again' click — rejected for this pass because it silently changes an existing surface's latency/cost profile (a zero-latency short-circuit would gain a live partner round trip) without the operator having decided that tradeoff; left as an explicit, separately-callable route instead, flagged for a deliberate decision.

Replacing horizen_pulse_authorized with the new fine-grained receipt types — rejected: it is the ONLY receipt several existing readers (the journey-state route's JOURNEY_ACTION_TYPES list, multiple tests) already depend on, and inv.engineering.036/037 forbids an unreviewed behavior change to an existing capability when an additive extension satisfies the same requirement.

Auto-issuing a revocation/expiry transition (e.g. PULSE_ENROLLMENT_REVOKED) directly from reconcilePulseConstitutionalState when a disagreement is found — rejected per the operator's own framing: 'that discrepancy itself becomes a new event requiring treatment — not an excuse to silently rewrite history'; a genuine state change is a separate, deliberate constitutional act, not something a read response gets to decide unilaterally.

Adding PULSE_HEALTH_VERIFIED and VERIFIABLE_PNL_VERIFIED action types now, alongside the two that were wired — rejected as speculative: neither has a real verified-event source in this codebase yet (no SLA-proof ingestion path, and Verifiable PnL is currently false for this pilot's live agent), and declaring an action type nothing ever issues is the half-finished-implementation CLAUDE.md's Change Sizing section forbids.
